section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, there are two aspects in G-d's statement to Moshe "when you lift up the head of the children of Israel": the literal lifting up, and the additional hidden aspect of raising the horn of Israel revealed through the Oral Torah.
section.t: And based on this, it can be said that in G-d's statement to Moshe, "When you lift up the head of the children of Israel,"
there are two matters.
[One is] that he should lift and raise the head of the children of Israel,
as is explicit in the verse.
And another matter
(which is not explicit in the Written Torah but is revealed in the Oral Torah),
that through "when you lift up the head of the children of Israel" there will also be a raising of the horn of Israel
[and as the language of the Gemara: "He said to him,
'When you lift up,'
that through 'when you lift up' there will be another matter].
And based on this, we can explain what Rashi said: "If you come to lift up their head in elevation, take from them an atonement for charity,"
and not "they shall give an atonement for charity,"
as the language of the verse, "And they shall give, each man, an atonement for his soul,"
because the lifting and elevation of the head of the children of Israel is through the giving of an atonement — "and they shall give, each man, an atonement for his soul."

And in order that the lifting of the head should bring about the raising of the horn of Israel, it is when the lifting and elevation of the head is through Moshe taking from them an atonement — "If you come to lift up their head in elevation, take from them an atonement for charity."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This is understood through the preface that the essence of G-d's desire is for kindness (chesed) and drawing down into the lower realms, which is the inner will, unlike sacrifices which are primarily an elevation from below to above.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is said
(in our parshah16)
"If you lend money to My people,"
and it is brought in the Midrash17
"Said the Holy One, blessed be He, 'If you lend money to My people'"
(with a chirik under the ayin, meaning "My people"),
and it is explained in the discourses18,
that this [teaches] that the virtue of gemilus chassadim (acts of lovingkindness) is so great that through this "you are My people,"
"My people in My partition"19,
as it is written20
"For I desire kindness, and not sacrifice,"
for although also the sacrifices
(sacrifice)
are His will, blessed be He,
[as is also understood from the fact that there are numerous commandments to offer sacrifices],
nevertheless,
since the matter of sacrifices is an elevation from below to above,
and the ultimate intention is that there should be a drawing down of the revelation of G-dliness below,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place in the lower realms21,
therefore,
the desire in sacrifices is
(not in the sacrifices in and of themselves,
but rather)
for the sake of the drawing down that will come afterwards through the libations
[as it is brought in the Gemara22
"Anyone who recites the Shema without tefillin is as if he offered a burnt-offering without a meal-offering and a peace-offering without libations"23,
for from this it is implied that when one offered a peace-offering without libations, his sacrifice is nothing24,
and it is explained in Likkutei Torah25
that this is because the elevation of the sacrifices is for the sake of the drawing down that follows through the libations],
and therefore,
the desire in sacrifices is
(like26)
the externality of the will
[comparable to27
a person who wants to travel to some place to buy merchandise,
that his desire in the journey is only for the profit he will have through it],
and the innerness of the will is in the drawing down below.
And this is [the meaning of] "For I desire kindness, and not sacrifice,"
that the desire,
the innerness of the will,
is that there should be kindness,
a drawing down below.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Even the drawing down through Torah is not as great as the drawing down through gemilus chassadim, which reaches down to this physical world.
section.t: And to add,
from the simple language of the verse "For I desire kindness, and not sacrifice," it implies that it speaks even of a sacrifice with libations,
and nevertheless it says "I desire kindness, and not sacrifice,"
because since the libations are secondary to the sacrifice,
even the drawing down through the libations is not like the drawing down through kindness.
And as is also proven from the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory28
(brought in the discourses29)
on the verse30
"If the iniquity of the house of Eli will be atoned with sacrifice and meal-offering,"
"With sacrifice and meal-offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned with Torah and gemilus chassadim,"
for even the atonement of the meal-offering
(and likewise libations)
is not like the atonement through Torah and gemilus chassadim,
because the entire matter of sacrifices is elevation,
except that within the sacrifices themselves — meal-offering and libations are a drawing down below,
but the drawing down through them is not like the drawing down through Torah and gemilus chassadim.
And furthermore,
even the drawing down of Torah,
which is called "Torah of kindness"31
because its matter is a drawing down below,
is not like the drawing down through kindness.
And as the conclusion of the aforementioned saying of our Rabbis28
"Rabbah, who engaged in Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who engaged in Torah and gemilus chassadim, lived sixty years."
And to note,
that this matter — that the drawing down through gemilus chassadim is a drawing down below more
(than the drawing down through meal-offering and libations, and also)
than the drawing down through Torah —
is in general [true] of all the mitzvos32,
for gemilus chassadim is the entirety of all the mitzvos33.
But nevertheless,
the primary virtue of the drawing down below the most is in gemilus chassadim in its simple sense.
And as is also understood from the continuation of the matters in the aforementioned discourses,
that the matter of "For I desire kindness, and not sacrifice" is an explanation of the virtue of "If you lend money,"
gemilus chassadim in its simple sense.
And so it is understood from what is explained in the aforementioned discourses34
the reason for this — that gemilus chassadim is among the things whose fruits a person eats in this world35,
because the drawing down through gemilus chassadim is drawn down to the very lowest,
also in this world.
